title: Engine will not start
fullDescription: Snapper riders and walk-behinds use B&S or Honda engines. Stale fuel and a fouled plug are the most common no-start issues after storage.

fixSteps.title: Fresh gas + plug
fixSteps.instruction: Drain and refill, install new plug.

fixSteps.title: Clean carb
fixSteps.instruction: Disassemble and clean if still no start.

title: Engine won't crank
fullDescription: Battery, cables, or interlocks. Snapper rear-engine riders also have a brake-pedal switch that must be fully depressed.

fixSteps.title: Press brake firmly
fixSteps.instruction: Snapper rear-engine requires hard brake press.

title: Blade engagement fails
shortDescription: PTO does not turn on the blades.
fullDescription: Older Snapper rear-engine models use a manual blade-engagement lever. Cable stretch or worn idler is the cause. Newer models with electric PTO follow the typical fuse / clutch troubleshooting.

title: Drive or deck belt slips
fullDescription: Glazed or stretched belts slip under load. Inspect both drive and deck belts.

title: Self-propel walk-behind doesn't drive
shortDescription: Bail engaged but mower doesn't pull itself.
fullDescription: Walk-behind self-propel uses a bail-actuated belt drive. Drive cable, belt, or transmission gear are common faults.

fixSteps.title: Adjust cable
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten drive cable to take up slack.

fixSteps.title: Replace belt
fixSteps.instruction: If still no drive, swap drive belt.

title: Uneven cut quality
fullDescription: Bent blade, deck level, or low tire — same as other riders.

title: Poor grass discharge
fullDescription: Dull blades, wet grass, or clogged deck.
